clue.text: Sweet and kindly disposed to the worker

parts.note: fond means affectionate, kindly disposed towards someone
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Someone is both sweet-natured and kind to the employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective describing a nice person, but it is the noun: a kind of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugary paste used as a confection or icing, so it is a type of sweet.

clue.text: One included in gross order

indicators.note: something included in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: gross in the sense of grossly overweight
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item is counted within an order of 144.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross order' suggests a bulk purchase of 144 items; here gross is FAT and order is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command, the noun sense of an order.

clue.text: Approach used in one argument

indicators.note: letters used in the following words are found inside them, spanning the word break

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A tactic is deployed within a single debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' reads as a noun meaning a method, but it is the verb: to come close.
explanation.definitionFit: To near a place is to draw closer to it, the verb sense of approach.

clue.text: Open and fit to support a new name

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged
in a down entry, what supports something sits beneath it, so this piece comes second

parts.note: the four letters of name rearranged
fit in the sense of capable

explanation.surface: A candid person is ready to back a fresh title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is receptive and willing to listen, which is to say open to suggestions.

clue.text: Care about river's flow

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to tend is to care for or look after
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone worries about how fast a river is running.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'flow' the river's current; it is the definition, a general drift.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is the general direction in which things are moving, their overall flow or drift.

clue.text: Search thoroughly before a time in battle

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next ones in the answer

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Soldiers sweep the ground thoroughly before the fighting starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting between armed forces, a synonym for battle as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Gold lace, possibly, for the fortune-teller

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement among many, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the letters of lace rearranged

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant might be offered golden lace as payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle, like the one at Delphi, was a person who foretold the future, a prophet or seer.

clue.text: Game to put money on? Nonsense!

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
gammon is old-fashioned British slang for nonsense or humbug

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of gambling on a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Gammon in the sense of nonsense is dated British slang, as in 'gammon and spinach'.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving pieces by dice throws.

clue.text: Enter Putin staggering with the paint mixture

indicators.note: something staggering lurches about unsteadily, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: all ten letters are used

explanation.surface: The Russian president lurches into a room carrying a pot of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a solvent mixed into oil paints to thin them, so it goes into a paint mixture.

clue.text: Literary places of learning made case for improvement

indicators.note: improving something means reworking it, so these letters are rearranged into a better form

parts.note: all eight letters are used

explanation.surface: Universities argue for more funding to better themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary' warns that academe is a bookish, poetic word for an academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is a literary word for an academy or university, a place where learning happens.

clue.text: Dish that could be flying, allegedly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small plate set under a cup
second meaning: the sort of craft people claim to have seen in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: The second half points to the 'flying' type that UFO witnesses report; 'allegedly' hints that nobody has proved one exists.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is a small dish under a cup, and a flying one is the supposed alien spacecraft.

clue.text: Notice a small cut, say, for a particularly beautiful kind of route

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the sounds of the pieces matter rather than their spelling

parts.note: to notice is to see
a nick is a small notch or cut

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tiny scratch while taking the pretty way home.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the two pieces run together as the answer; the 'scenic route' is the picturesque way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic describes a place with attractive natural views, so it means particularly beautiful.

clue.text: Sent, it is said, bottled water from Germany

definitions.note: a soundalike for scent, the real definition

indicators.note: it is said means spoken aloud, so the preceding word stands for one that sounds the same

parts.note: first meaning, by sound: a perfume
second meaning: the French name translates as water of Cologne, a German city

explanation.surface: Someone has dispatched a consignment of German mineral water, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' is a stand-in for scent, which sounds the same; the second half translates the French name literally, since Cologne is in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light perfume, a scent, first made in Cologne and sold in bottles.

clue.text: Remove what should be left by right

definitions.text: Remove what should be left by right

parts.words: Remove what should be left by right
parts.note: surface reading: take away something that, properly, ought to stay where it is
setter's reading: left means bequeathed in a will, so this is cutting someone off from what they would rightfully inherit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left by right' plays on left versus right, but left here means handed down in a will, and 'by right' means rightfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to deprive an heir of the inheritance that would normally pass to them.

clue.text: Leave in a French plant is not reciprocated

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the plant that follows

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass
to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: A foliage leaf left inside a French plant gets nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Leave' as foliage; it is the verb, to depart, sitting inside the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrequited love is love not returned by its object, so unrequited means not reciprocated.

clue.text: Bondsman?

parts.note: surface reading: a bondsman is a serf or slave, or one who stands surety
setter's reading: Bond's man, the writer responsible for the spy James Bond

explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as Bond's man and you get the author who created 007.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming was the British novelist who created the secret agent James Bond.

clue.text: Environment of place beneath a motorway

indicators.note: in a down entry, beneath puts this piece below the one that follows it in the clue

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written with I for 1
lieu is French for place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: The surroundings of a spot under a motorway bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is the social setting or surroundings someone lives in, their environment.

clue.text: Check-up that's just the word in Paris

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the annual roadworthiness test for British cars
second meaning: ... is French for word, as in le ... juste

explanation.walkthrough: The MOT, named for the old Ministry of Transport, is the yearly safety test British cars must pass. 'Just the word' nods to le mot juste.
explanation.definitionFit: The MOT is a vehicle inspection, a check-up for a car, and mot is the French noun for word.

clue.text: Sporting type involved in deadlock?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... half, a rugby position also called fly-half
second meaning: a stalemate where neither side gives way

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the stand-off (fly-half) is the player who receives the ball from the scrum-half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a standoff between opponents, a deadlock, and also the name of a rugby player's position.

clue.text: Declaration when not out? That's cool!

parts.note: 'I see!' is what you declare when something is not out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a narrow escape with relaxed approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is signalled only by the question mark; 'not out' sounds like cricket but means in view.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice something is to chill it, so ice works as the verb cool.

clue.text: Depressed by difficulty leading to a walking stick

parts.note: a black mood is a depressed one
a thorn in one's side is a persistent difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone worn down by problems ends up needing a stick to walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackthorn wood is the traditional material for a walking stick or shillelagh, so the stick takes the shrub's name.

clue.text: Feel deep respect for Paul, the patriot

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the American silversmith famous for his midnight ride in 1775

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as admiring a man named Paul; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to venerate, and Paul Revere was the American revolutionary hero of the midnight ride.

clue.text: Money required for Home Affairs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the household budget for food and bills
second meaning: the running of a home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Home Affairs' suggests the government department (the Home Office), but it means domestic chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Housekeeping is both the management of a household and the allowance of cash set aside for running it.

clue.text: Physicist friend accompanying one round the university

indicators.note: accompanying puts the pieces side by side, one following the other
round means surrounding, so the friend wraps about the next item

parts.note: a pal is a friend
U is the abbreviation for university
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scientist's companion walks with someone around the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Pauli was the Austrian physicist known for the exclusion principle in quantum mechanics.

clue.text: The extent of preparation for the wall?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a thin glue brushed on a wall before papering

explanation.walkthrough: Size is also a gelatinous sealant painted onto plaster so wallpaper paste grips; the surface reads like measuring a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Size means extent or magnitude, and size is also the glaze applied to walls to prepare them for paper.

clue.text: Boss to consult the books endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to study is to pore over books

explanation.surface: A manager keeps checking the accounts without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it means a round knob or projection, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, and a stud is a similar decorative stud or knob.

clue.text: Quite pretty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fairly, to some degree
second meaning: the adverb, as in 'pretty good'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite pretty' reads as mild praise for someone's looks; both words are adverbs of degree here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, quite and pretty are all adverbs meaning moderately or to a fair degree.

clue.text: I can be funny thus about the pollsters

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the following word is read in an odd order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged word wraps round the pollsters

parts.note: the four letters of thus rearranged
MORI is a British opinion-polling company, now Ipsos

explanation.surface: A comedian jokes about opinion-poll companies.
explanation.walkthrough: MORI (Market and Opinion Research International) is a well-known British polling firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorist is a comic writer or performer, someone who can say 'I can be funny'.

clue.text: Arranged things when it reversed and stopped

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word it follows is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
an engine that died stopped running

explanation.surface: A car's engine reversed and stalled, so its owner sorted things out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidied means put things in order, which is to arrange them neatly.

clue.text: Bull may be seen here — an area well inside the boundary

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: a bull is seen in a field

definitions.text: an area well inside the boundary
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the cricket fielding area near the pitch, away from the rope

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words to get where a bull grazes; in cricket the whole word is the inner part of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The infield in cricket is the region close to the wicket, well within the boundary rope at the edge.
